title: Open WebUI knowledge search -- T1499 unbounded backtracking regex pins a worker for as long as the attacker wants
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70493 (GHSA-2f54-p244-32q6,
CVSS 6.5 MEDIUM), affecting Open WebUI's default-enabled built-in
`grep_knowledge_files` tool.

`build_matcher()` in `backend/open_webui/tools/knowledge_fs.py`
treats any caller-supplied pattern containing regex metacharacters as
a regex, compiles it with Python's backtracking `re` engine, and
returns an unbounded match function with no time limit anywhere on
the path. `grep_knowledge_files()` in `builtin.py` -- the default
handler an LLM reaches with `ENABLE_KB_EXEC` at its default `False` --
runs that matcher over every line of every reachable file
synchronously inside the event loop. A pattern like `(x|x)*y` against
a crafted subject line grows exponentially with subject length --
measured on the vulnerable code, 24 characters takes 1.2s, 28 takes
19s, 30 takes 74s -- and because it runs on the shared event loop, one
crafted search pins a CPU core and starves every other request the
worker is serving, not just the attacker's own.

Detection logic flags a knowledge-search tool invocation whose pattern
argument contains alternation combined with a repetition quantifier
applied to a group -- the exact overlapping-construct shape (e.g.
`(x|x)*`) this advisory's catastrophic-backtracking finding
demonstrates, against the tool this corpus's `builtin.py` handler
reaches by default.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact function names, source files, and a
reproducible growth table), fixed in 0.11.0.
